framework_name: FedRAMP Requirements — provider-facing rules (Consolidated Rules for 2026)

controls.title: Acknowledge Receipt
controls.description: Providers SHOULD promptly and automatically acknowledge the receipt of messages received from FedRAMP in their FedRAMP Security Inbox.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: FedRAMP Security Inbox, Promptly, Provider.

controls.title: Complete Required Actions
controls.description: Providers MUST complete the required actions in Emergency or Emergency Test designated messages sent by FedRAMP within the timeframe included in the message.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): Timeframes may vary by FedRAMP Certification class.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Class, Provider.

controls.title: Emergency Message Routing
controls.description: Providers MUST route Emergency designated messages sent by FedRAMP to a senior security official for their awareness.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): Senior security officials are determined by the provider.

Related FedRAMP terms: Provider.

controls.title: Important Message Actions
controls.description: Providers SHOULD complete the required actions in Important designated messages sent by FedRAMP within the timeframe specified in the message.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): Timeframes may vary by FedRAMP Certification class.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Class, Provider.

controls.title: Maintain a FedRAMP Security Inbox
controls.description: Providers MUST establish and maintain an email address to receive messages from FedRAMP; this inbox is a FedRAMP Security Inbox (FSI).
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: FedRAMP Security Inbox, Provider.

controls.title: Notification of Changes
controls.description: Providers MUST immediately notify FedRAMP of any changes to the email address for their FedRAMP Security Inbox.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: FedRAMP Security Inbox, Provider.

controls.title: Receive Email Without Disruption
controls.description: Providers MUST receive and react to email messages from FedRAMP without disruption and without requiring additional actions from FedRAMP.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): This requirement is intended to prevent cloud service providers from requiring FedRAMP to complete a CAPTCHA, log into a customer portal, or otherwise take service-specific actions that might prevent the security team from receiving the message.

Related FedRAMP terms: Provider.

controls.title: Trust @fedramp.gov and @gsa.gov
controls.description: Providers MUST treat any email originating from an @fedramp.gov or @gsa.gov email address as if it was sent from FedRAMP by default; if such a message is confirmed to originate from someone other than FedRAMP then the FedRAMP Security Inbox rules no longer apply.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: FedRAMP Security Inbox, Provider.

controls.title: Anonymized Feedback Summary
controls.description: Providers MUST supply an anonymized and desensitized summary of the feedback, questions, and answers about each Ongoing Certification Report as an addendum to the Ongoing Certification Report OR in the next Ongoing Certification Report.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): This is intended to encourage sharing of information and decrease the burden on the cloud service provider - providing this summary will reduce duplicate questions from agencies and ensure FedRAMP has access to this information. It is generally in the provider's interest to update this addendum frequently throughout the quarter.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, FedRAMP Certification Report, Ongoing Certification, Ongoing Certification Report (OCR), Provider.

controls.title: Report Availability
controls.description: Providers MUST supply an Ongoing Certification Report to all necessary parties every 3 months, covering the entire period since the previous summary, in a consistent format that is human readable; this report MUST include high-level summaries of at least the following information:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- Changes to FedRAMP Certification Data
- Planned changes to FedRAMP Certification Data during at least the next 3 months
- Accepted vulnerabilities
- Transformative changes
- Updated recommendations or best practices for security, configuration, usage, or similar aspects of the cloud service offering
- A list of all agencies that are directly using the product
- FedRAMP Reportable Incidents or an attestation that no such incidents occurred
- Lessons learned and changes planned or made as a result of FedRAMP Reportable Incidents (if such occurred)

Related FedRAMP terms: Accepted Vulnerability, Agency, All Necessary Parties, Certification Data, Cloud Service Offering, FedRAMP Certification Report, FedRAMP Reportable Incident, Incident, Ongoing Certification, Ongoing Certification Report (OCR), Provider, Transformative Change, Vulnerability.

Machine-readable schema: https://fedramp.gov/schemas/fedramp-ongoing-certification-report-schema-2026-06-24.json

controls.title: Feedback Mechanism
controls.description: Providers MUST supply an asynchronous mechanism for all necessary parties to provide feedback or ask questions about each Ongoing Certification Report.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): This could be email by default but providers are encouraged to consider something more interactive as appropriate.

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, FedRAMP Certification Report, Ongoing Certification, Ongoing Certification Report (OCR), Provider.

controls.title: Limit Sensitive Information
controls.description: Providers MUST NOT irresponsibly disclose sensitive information in an Ongoing Certification Report that would likely have an adverse effect on the cloud service offering.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST NOT.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Cloud Service Offering, FedRAMP Certification Report, Likely, Ongoing Certification, Ongoing Certification Report (OCR), Provider.

controls.title: Next Report Date
controls.description: Providers MUST supply the target date for their next Ongoing Certification Report with other public FedRAMP Certification Data.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Data, FedRAMP Certification Report, Ongoing Certification, Ongoing Certification Report (OCR), Provider.

controls.title: Responsible Public Certification Report Sharing
controls.description: Providers MAY responsibly supply some or all of the information an Ongoing Certification Report to the public or other parties if the provider determines doing so will NOT likely have an adverse effect on the cloud service offering.
controls.guidance:
Force: MAY.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Cloud Service Offering, FedRAMP Certification Report, Likely, Ongoing Certification, Ongoing Certification Report (OCR), Provider, Responsibly.

controls.title: Spread Out Reports
controls.description: Providers SHOULD establish a regular 3 month cycle for Ongoing Certification Reports that is spread out from the beginning, middle, or end of each quarter.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): This recommendation is intended to discourage hundreds of cloud service providers from releasing their Ongoing Certification Reports during the first or last week of each quarter because that is the easiest way for a single provider to track this deliverable; the result would overwhelm agencies with many cloud services. Widely used cloud service providers are encouraged to work with their customers to identify ideal timeframes for this cycle.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Ongoing Certification, Provider, Regularly.

controls.title: Additional Content
controls.description: Providers SHOULD supply additional information in Quarterly Reviews that the provider determines is of interest, use, or otherwise relevant to agencies.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Provider, Quarterly Review.

controls.title: Quarterly Review Meeting
controls.description: Providers with Class C Certifications MUST host a synchronous Quarterly Review every 3 months, open to all necessary parties, to review aspects of the most recent Ongoing Certification Reports that the provider determines are of the most relevance to agencies.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Class-A variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MAY): Providers with Class A Certifications MAY host a synchronous Quarterly Review every 3 months, open to all necessary parties, to review aspects of the most recent Ongoing Certification Reports that the provider determines are of the most relevance to agencies.

Class-B variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force SHOULD): Providers with Class B Certifications SHOULD host a synchronous Quarterly Review every 3 months, open to all necessary parties, to review aspects of the most recent Ongoing Certification Reports that the provider determines are of the most relevance to agencies.

Class-C variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Class C Certifications MUST host a synchronous Quarterly Review every 3 months, open to all necessary parties, to review aspects of the most recent Ongoing Certification Reports that the provider determines are of the most relevance to agencies.

Class-D variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Class D Certifications MUST host a synchronous Quarterly Review every 3 months, open to all necessary parties, to review aspects of the most recent Ongoing Certification Reports that the provider determines are of the most relevance to agencies.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, All Necessary Parties, Ongoing Certification, Provider, Quarterly Review.

controls.title: No Irresponsible Disclosure
controls.description: Providers MUST NOT irresponsibly disclose sensitive information in a Quarterly Review that would likely have an adverse effect on the cloud service offering.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST NOT.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Cloud Service Offering, Likely, Provider, Quarterly Review.

controls.title: Next Review Date
controls.description: Providers MUST publicly supply the target date for their next Quarterly Review with other public FedRAMP Certification Data.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Data, Provider, Quarterly Review.

controls.title: Meeting Registration Info
controls.description: Providers MUST supply either a registration link or a downloadable calendar file with meeting information for Quarterly Reviews to all necessary parties.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, Provider, Quarterly Review.

controls.title: Restrict Third Parties
controls.description: Providers SHOULD NOT invite third parties to attend Quarterly Reviews intended for agencies unless they have specific relevance.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD NOT.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): This is because agencies are less likely to actively participate in meetings with third parties; the cloud service provider's independent assessor should be considered relevant by default.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Assessor, Likely, Provider, Quarterly Review.

controls.title: Record/Transcribe Reviews
controls.description: Providers SHOULD record or transcribe Quarterly Reviews and supply them to all necessary parties.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, Provider, Quarterly Review.

controls.title: Schedule Around Reports
controls.description: Providers SHOULD regularly schedule Quarterly Reviews to occur at least 3 business days after releasing an Ongoing Certification Report AND within 10 business days of such release.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: FedRAMP Certification Report, Ongoing Certification, Ongoing Certification Report (OCR), Provider, Quarterly Review, Regularly.

controls.title: Share Content Responsibly
controls.description: Providers MAY responsibly supply content prepared for a Quarterly Review to the public or other parties if the provider determines doing so will NOT likely have an adverse effect on the cloud service offering.
controls.guidance:
Force: MAY.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Cloud Service Offering, Likely, Provider, Quarterly Review, Responsibly.

controls.title: Share Recordings Responsibly
controls.description: Providers MAY responsibly supply recordings or transcriptions of Quarterly Reviews to the public or other parties ONLY if the provider removes all agency information (comments, questions, names, etc.) AND determines doing so will NOT likely have an adverse effect on the cloud service offering.
controls.guidance:
Force: MAY.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Cloud Service Offering, Likely, Provider, Quarterly Review, Responsibly.

controls.title: Trust Center Migration
controls.description: Providers MUST notify all necessary parties when migrating to a trust center and MUST provide information in their existing USDA Connect Community Portal secure folders explaining how to use the trust center to obtain FedRAMP Certification Data.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to FedRAMP Rev 5 authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, Certification Data, Provider, Trust Center.

controls.title: Availability Reporting
controls.description: Providers with Class C Certifications MUST maintain a web service, available to all necessary parties, that indicates current and historical availability of core services within the cloud service offering over at least the past 30 days, including availability incidents, in both human-readable and machine-readable formats; this service MUST be available even if the primary cloud service offering is unavailable.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Class-A variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force SHOULD): Providers with Class A Certifications SHOULD maintain a web service, available to all necessary parties, that indicates current and historical availability of core services within the cloud service offering over at least the past 30 days, including availability incidents, in both human-readable and machine-readable formats; this service SHOULD be available even if the primary cloud service offering is unavailable.

Class-B variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Class B Certifications MUST maintain a web service, available to all necessary parties, that indicates current and historical availability of core services within the cloud service offering over at least the past 30 days, including availability incidents, in both human-readable and machine-readable formats; this service MUST be available even if the primary cloud service offering is unavailable.

Class-C variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Class C Certifications MUST maintain a web service, available to all necessary parties, that indicates current and historical availability of core services within the cloud service offering over at least the past 30 days, including availability incidents, in both human-readable and machine-readable formats; this service MUST be available even if the primary cloud service offering is unavailable.

Class-D variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Class D Certifications MUST maintain a web service, available to all necessary parties, that indicates current and historical availability of core services within the cloud service offering over at least the past 30 days, including availability incidents, in both human-readable and machine-readable formats; this service MUST be available even if the primary cloud service offering is unavailable.

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, Cloud Service Offering, Incident, Machine-Readable, Provider.

controls.title: Consistency Between Formats
controls.description: Providers MUST use automation to ensure information remains consistent between human-readable and machine-readable formats when FedRAMP Certification Data is provided in both formats.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Data, Machine-Readable, Provider.

controls.title: Always Include FedRAMP ID
controls.description: Providers MUST always include the FedRAMP ID of the related cloud service offering in all FedRAMP Certification Data once assigned, including all reports, notifications, and other communication that results from FedRAMP rules.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Data, Cloud Service Offering, Provider.

controls.title: FedRAMP Certification Reports
controls.description: Providers MUST include FedRAMP Certification Reports with their FedRAMP Certification Data without inappropriate modifications, and make such reports available within 2 weeks of receiving the materials from FedRAMP.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): FedRAMP provides Certification Reports for all cloud service offerings following the Program Certification path as part of the initial and ongoing FedRAMP Certification process, and may provide Certification Reports for cloud service offerings following the Agency Certification path.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Certification Data, Certification Path, Cloud Service Offering, Provider.

controls.title: Historical FedRAMP Certification Data
controls.description: Providers MUST supply snapshots of FedRAMP Certification Data aligned to Ongoing Certification Reports to all necessary parties; these snapshots MUST be available for the duration of FedRAMP Certification.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): Historical snapshots do not need to be reconstructed for periods before the provider's first Ongoing Certification Report, but should be maintained for all subsequent Ongoing Certification Reports.

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, Certification Data, FedRAMP Certification Report, Ongoing Certification, Ongoing Certification Report (OCR), Provider.

controls.title: Include Relevant Policies
controls.description: Providers MUST supply all relevant policies and procedures in the FedRAMP Certification Data, including a human-readable and machine-readable reference that explains at least the following about each included policy and procedure:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- Name of policy or procedure
- Name of file, document, web page, etc.
- Brief summary of policy or procedure
- Word count of document
- Current version
- Date of last update
- Related FedRAMP Practices (if applicable)

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Data, FedRAMP Practices, Machine-Readable, Provider.

controls.title: Per-Service Certification Materials
controls.description: Providers with Class C Certifications MAY supply per-service FedRAMP Certification materials.
controls.guidance:
Force: MAY.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Class-A variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MAY): Providers with Class A Certifications MAY supply per-service FedRAMP Certification materials.

Class-B variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MAY): Providers with Class B Certifications MAY supply per-service FedRAMP Certification materials.

Class-C variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MAY): Providers with Class C Certifications MAY supply per-service FedRAMP Certification materials.

Class-D variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Class D Certifications MUST supply per-service FedRAMP Certification materials.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Provider.

controls.title: Public Information
controls.description: Providers MUST publicly share up-to-date information about the cloud service offering in both human-readable and JSON formats, including at least the following information that is available and applicable:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- FedRAMP ID
- Service Model
- Deployment Model
- Business Category
- UEI Number
- Sales Contact Information
- Security Contact Information
- Product Website Link
- Link to Product Logo
- Overall Service Description
- Detailed list of specific services and their security categories (see CDS-CSO-SVC (Public Service List) (Service List))
- Link to Secure Configuration Guidance
- Overview of documentation supplied by the provider for the cloud service offering
- Link to Trust Center landing page that includes instructions on accessing information in the trust center
- Next Ongoing Certification Report date (see CCM-OCR-NRD (Next Report Date))
- Current FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service

Upstream note (verbatim): Generally, this information should be available on a public webpage or publicly shared in a FedRAMP-compatible trust center.

Related FedRAMP terms: Cloud Service Offering, FedRAMP Certification Report, FedRAMP Recognized, Ongoing Certification, Ongoing Certification Report (OCR), Provider, Security Category, Trust Center.

Machine-readable schema: https://fedramp.gov/schemas/fedramp-certification-package-overview-schema-2026-06-24.json

controls.title: Responsible Information Sharing
controls.description: Providers MUST provide sufficient information in FedRAMP Certification Data to support agency authorization decisions but SHOULD NOT include sensitive information that would likely enable a threat actor to gain unauthorized access, cause harm, disrupt operations, or otherwise have a negative adverse impact on the cloud service offering.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): This is not a license to exclude accurate risk information, but specifics that would likely lead to compromise should be abstracted. A breach of confidentiality with FedRAMP Certification Data should be anticipated by a secure cloud service provider.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Certification Data, Cloud Service Offering, Likely, Provider.

controls.title: Responsible Public Package Sharing
controls.description: Providers MAY responsibly share some or all of the information in a FedRAMP Certification Package publicly or with other parties if the provider determines doing so will NOT likely have an adverse effect on the cloud service offering.
controls.guidance:
Force: MAY.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Package, Cloud Service Offering, Likely, Provider, Responsibly.

controls.title: Public Service List
controls.description: Providers MUST publicly share a detailed list of specific services and their security categories that are included in the cloud service offering using clear feature or service names that align with standard public marketing materials; this list MUST be complete enough for a potential customer to determine which services are and are not included in the FedRAMP Minimum Assessment Scope without requesting access to underlying FedRAMP Certification Data.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Data, Cloud Service Offering, Provider, Security Category.

Machine-readable schema: https://fedramp.gov/schemas/fedramp-certification-package-overview-schema-2026-06-24.json

controls.title: Use Trust Centers
controls.description: Providers MUST use a FedRAMP-compatible trust center to store and share FedRAMP Certification Data with all necessary parties.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): Rules for FedRAMP-Compatible Trust Centers are explained in the Certification Data Sharing Rules under the FedRAMP-Compatible Trust Centers section (id: CDS-TRC).

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, Certification Data, Provider, Trust Center.

Machine-readable schema: https://fedramp.gov/schemas/fedramp-certification-package-overview-schema-2026-06-24.json

controls.title: Agency Access Inventory
controls.description: Trust centers MUST maintain an inventory and history of federal agency users or systems with access to FedRAMP Certification Data and MUST make this information available to FedRAMP upon request.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Certification Data, Trust Center.

controls.title: Access Logging
controls.description: Trust centers MUST log access to FedRAMP Certification Data and store summaries of access for at least six months; such information, as it pertains to specific parties, SHOULD be made available upon request by those parties.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Data, Trust Center.

controls.title: Human and Machine-Readable Certification Data
controls.description: Trust centers SHOULD make FedRAMP Certification Data available to view and download in both human-readable and machine-readable formats.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Data, Machine-Readable, Trust Center.

controls.title: Programmatic Access
controls.description: Trust centers MUST provide documented programmatic access to all FedRAMP Certification Data, including programmatic access to human-readable materials.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Data, Trust Center.

controls.title: Self-Service Access Management
controls.description: Trust centers SHOULD include features that encourage all necessary parties to provision and manage access to FedRAMP Certification Data for their users and services directly.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, Certification Data, Trust Center.

controls.title: Uninterrupted Sharing
controls.description: Trust centers MUST share FedRAMP Certification Data with all necessary parties without interruption.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): "Without interruption" means that parties should not have to request manual approval each time they need to access FedRAMP Certification Data or go through a complicated process. The preferred way of ensuring access without interruption is to use on-demand just-in-time access provisioning.

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, Certification Data, Trust Center.

controls.title: Agency Access Denial
controls.description: Providers MUST notify FedRAMP within 5 business days of denying an agency access request for FedRAMP Certification Data.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Certification Data, Provider.

controls.title: Agency Access
controls.description: Providers SHOULD supply access to the FedRAMP Certification Package with agencies upon request.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Certification Package, Provider.

controls.title: Configuration of Agency Tenants
controls.description: Providers SHOULD configure agency tenants by default to use cryptographic services that use cryptographic modules or update streams of cryptographic modules with active validations under the NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program when such modules are available.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Provider, Validation.

controls.title: Cryptographic Module Documentation
controls.description: Providers MUST document the cryptographic modules used in each service (or groups of services that use the same modules) where cryptographic services are used to protect federal customer data, including whether these modules are validated under the NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program or are update streams of such modules.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Federal Customer Data, Provider, Validation.

controls.title: Using Validated Cryptographic Modules
controls.description: Providers with Class C Certifications SHOULD use cryptographic modules or update streams of cryptographic modules with active validations under the NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program when using cryptographic services to protect federal customer data.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Class-A variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MAY): Providers with Class A Certifications MAY use cryptographic modules or update streams of cryptographic modules with active validations under the NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program when using cryptographic services to protect federal customer data.

Class-B variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MAY): Providers with Class B Certifications MAY use cryptographic modules or update streams of cryptographic modules with active validations under the NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program when using cryptographic services to protect federal customer data.

Class-C variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force SHOULD): Providers with Class C Certifications SHOULD use cryptographic modules or update streams of cryptographic modules with active validations under the NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program when using cryptographic services to protect federal customer data.

Class-D variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Class D Certifications MUST use cryptographic modules or update streams of cryptographic modules with active validations under the NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program when using cryptographic services to protect federal customer data.

Related FedRAMP terms: Federal Customer Data, Provider, Validation.

controls.title: Certification Package Maintenance for Rev5
controls.description: Providers with Rev5 Class C Certifications MUST persistently maintain their FedRAMP Certification Package to ensure it is up to date and complete at least once every year.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to FedRAMP Rev 5 authorizations.

Class-B variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Rev5 Class B Certifications MUST persistently maintain their FedRAMP Certification Package to ensure it is up to date and complete at least once every year.

Class-C variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Rev5 Class C Certifications MUST persistently maintain their FedRAMP Certification Package to ensure it is up to date and complete at least once every year.

Class-D variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Rev5 Class D Certifications MUST persistently maintain their FedRAMP Certification Package to ensure it is up to date and complete at least once every six months.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Package, Persistently, Provider, Significant Change, Transformative Change.

controls.title: Certification Package Overview Metadata
controls.description: Providers MUST also include the following basic metadata in their Certification Package Overview:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- Name, title, and contact information of official that is responsible and accountable for the FedRAMP Certification Package
- Version
- Date and time of last update
- Source of update

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Package, Provider.

controls.title: Overall Summary of Assessment in Certification Package
controls.description: Providers seeking Class C Certification MUST also include the overall summary of their FedRAMP independent assessment, supplied by the assessor per IVV-IAS-OSA (Overall Summary of Assessment), in their Certification Package Overview.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Class-A variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MAY): Providers seeking Class A Certification MAY also include an overall summary of their FedRAMP independent assessment in their Certification Package Overview.

Class-B variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers seeking Class B Certification MUST also include the overall summary of their FedRAMP independent assessment, supplied by the assessor per IVV-IAS-OSA (Overall Summary of Assessment), in their Certification Package Overview.

Class-C variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers seeking Class C Certification MUST also include the overall summary of their FedRAMP independent assessment, supplied by the assessor per IVV-IAS-OSA (Overall Summary of Assessment), in their Certification Package Overview.

Class-D variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers seeking Class D Certification MUST also include the overall summary of their FedRAMP independent assessment, supplied by the assessor per IVV-IAS-OSA (Overall Summary of Assessment), in their Certification Package Overview.

controls.title: Assessment of Rev5 Controls with Findings
controls.description: Providers MUST have Rev5 Controls with negative findings from the previous FedRAMP independent assessment included in the next FedRAMP independent assessment.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to FedRAMP Rev 5 authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: FedRAMP Independent Assessment, Provider.

controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to FedRAMP Rev 5 authorizations.

Class-B variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Rev5 Class B Certifications MUST include the following Rev5 Controls in a FedRAMP independent assessment at least once per year:

Class-C variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Rev5 Class C Certifications MUST include the following Rev5 Controls in a FedRAMP independent assessment at least once per year:

Class-D variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Rev5 Class D Certifications MUST include the following Rev5 Controls in a FedRAMP independent assessment at least once per year:

controls.title: Mandatory Control Assessment
controls.description: Providers MUST have all applicable Rev5 Controls included in FedRAMP independent assessments every 3 years but are not required to have all Rev5 Controls included in the same FedRAMP independent assessment.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to FedRAMP Rev 5 authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): Traditionally this has been done by reviewing a rotating selection of Rev5 Controls at each annual assessment, however this requirement is a ceiling and not a floor. See IVV-CSF-PCA (Preferred Control Assessment) for FedRAMP's recommended approach to Rev5 control assessments.

Related FedRAMP terms: FedRAMP Independent Assessment, Provider.

controls.title: Preferred Control Assessment
controls.description: Providers SHOULD include all applicable Rev5 Controls in each FedRAMP independent assessment.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to FedRAMP Rev 5 authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: FedRAMP Independent Assessment, Provider.

controls.title: Document Use of Representative Samples
controls.description: Providers MUST document and explain the use of representative samples during verification and validation when using representative samples as allowed by IVV-CSO-USR (Use Representative Samples).
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Provider, Validation, Verification.

controls.title: FedRAMP Independent Assessments
controls.description: Providers with Class C Certifications MUST persistently complete an independent verification and validation assessment of all applicable FedRAMP rules with a FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service OR FedRAMP at least once per year; this is a FedRAMP independent assessment.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Class-A variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MAY): Providers with Class A Certifications MAY persistently complete an independent verification and validation assessment of all applicable FedRAMP rules with a FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service OR FedRAMP at least once per year; this is a FedRAMP independent assessment.

Class-B variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Class B Certifications MUST persistently complete an independent verification and validation assessment of all applicable FedRAMP rules with a FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service OR FedRAMP at least once per year; this is a FedRAMP independent assessment.

Class-C variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Class C Certifications MUST persistently complete an independent verification and validation assessment of all applicable FedRAMP rules with a FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service OR FedRAMP at least once per year; this is a FedRAMP independent assessment.

Class-D variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with Class D Certifications MUST persistently complete an independent verification and validation assessment of all applicable FedRAMP rules with a FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service OR FedRAMP at least once per year; this is a FedRAMP independent assessment.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Class, FedRAMP Independent Assessment, FedRAMP Recognized, Persistently, Provider, Validation, Verification.

controls.title: Inclusion in Certification Package
controls.description: Providers MUST supply the results of FedRAMP independent assessments in their FedRAMP Certification Package without inappropriate modification.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Package, FedRAMP Independent Assessment, Provider, Verification.

controls.title: Receiving Assessor Advice
controls.description: Providers MAY ask for and accept advice from their assessor during assessment regarding techniques and procedures that will improve their security posture or the effectiveness, clarity, and accuracy of their verification, validation and reporting procedures, UNLESS doing so is likely to compromise the objectivity and integrity of the assessment.
controls.guidance:
Force: MAY.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Assessor, Likely, Provider, Validation, Verification.

controls.title: Supply Evidence of Effectiveness
controls.description: Providers MUST supply evidence to all necessary assessors of the effectiveness of the measures that have been implemented to meet FedRAMP Practices; this evidence is the result of validation.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): For example, after verifying that firewalls are configured to block traffic following IVV-CSO-SEI (Supply Evidence of Implementation), the provider would validate that traffic is actually being blocked and supply evidence of that validation to assessors (such as by allowing them to see metrics on the traffic that is blocked vs not).

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Assessors, Assessor, FedRAMP Practices, Provider, Validation.

controls.title: Supply Evidence of Implementation
controls.description: Providers MUST supply evidence to all necessary assessors of the implementation of the measures that have been documented to meet FedRAMP Practices; this evidence is the result of verification.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): For example, if the documentation says that firewall rules are used to block traffic then the cloud service provider would verify that firewall rules are in place to block traffic and supply that evidence to assessors (preferably by allowing them to see how firewall configurations are deployed from a source of truth).

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Assessors, Assessor, FedRAMP Practices, Provider, Verification.

controls.title: Supply Technical Explanations
controls.description: Providers SHOULD supply all necessary assessors with technical explanations, demonstrations, and other relevant supporting information about the technical capabilities they employ to address FedRAMP rules; this SHOULD be supplied as necessary to ensure the assessor can effectively complete verification and validation.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Assessors, Assessor, Provider, Validation, Verification.

controls.title: Use Representative Samples
controls.description: Providers MAY use representative samples as appropriate during verification and validation.
controls.guidance:
Force: MAY.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): Many modern cloud services using effective automation do not need to use representative sampling and are capable of persistently verifying and validating the majority of their security measures automatically.

Related FedRAMP terms: Persistently, Provider, Validation, Verification.

controls.title: Annual Independent Assessments for 20x
controls.description: Providers with 20x Class C Certifications MUST include all Key Security Indicators in a FedRAMP independent assessment at least once per year.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to FedRAMP 20x authorizations.

Class-A variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with 20x Class A Certifications MUST meet the expectations of their underlying alternative security framework as part of their persistent independent verification and validation assessment.

Class-B variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with 20x Class B Certifications MUST include all Key Security Indicators in a FedRAMP independent assessment at least once per year.

Class-C variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with 20x Class C Certifications MUST include all Key Security Indicators in a FedRAMP independent assessment at least once per year.

Class-D variant (upstream `varies_by_class`, verbatim; force MUST): Providers with 20x Class D Certifications MUST include all Key Security Indicators in a FedRAMP independent assessment at least once per year.

Related FedRAMP terms: FedRAMP Independent Assessment, Persistently, Provider, Validation, Verification.

controls.title: Information Flows and Security Categories
controls.description: Providers MUST clearly identify, document, and explain information flows and security categories for ALL information resources or sets of information resources in the cloud service offering.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): Information resources (including third-party information resources) MAY vary by security category as appropriate to the type of information handled by or impacted by the information resource.

Related FedRAMP terms: Cloud Service Offering, Handle, Information Resource, Provider, Security Category, Third-Party Information Resource.

controls.title: Identify Information Resources
controls.description: Providers MUST identify a set of information resources to assess for FedRAMP Certification that includes all information resources that are likely to handle federal customer data or likely to impact the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of federal customer data handled by the cloud service offering; this set of information resources is the cloud service offering.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Certification Package, Cloud Service Offering, Federal Customer Data, Handle, Information Resource, Likely, Provider.

controls.title: Metadata Inclusion
controls.description: Providers MUST include metadata (including metadata about federal customer data) in the Minimum Assessment Scope ONLY IF MAS-CSO-IIR (Identify Information Resources) APPLIES.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Federal Customer Data, Information Resource, Initial Incident Report (IIR), Provider.

controls.title: Supplemental Information
controls.description: Providers MAY include additional materials about other information resources that are not part of the cloud service offering in a FedRAMP Certification Package supplement; these resources will not be FedRAMP Certified and MUST be clearly marked and separated from the cloud service offering.
controls.guidance:
Force: MAY.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): This is intended to allow inclusion of things like security materials for apps, supplemental marketing collateral, and other information that is not part of the cloud service offering but may be useful to agencies.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Certification Package, Cloud Service Offering, FedRAMP Certified, Information Resource, Provider.

controls.title: Third-Party Information Resources
controls.description: Providers MUST address the potential impact to federal customer data from third-party information resources used by the cloud service offering, ONLY IF MAS-CSO-IIR (Identify Information Resources) APPLIES, by documenting the following information about each applicable third-party information resource:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- General usage and configuration
- Explanation or justification for use
- Mitigation measures in place to reduce the potential impact to federal customer data
- Compensating controls in place to reduce the potential impact to federal customer data

Related FedRAMP terms: Cloud Service Offering, Federal Customer Data, Information Resource, Initial Incident Report (IIR), Provider, Third-Party Information Resource.

controls.title: Marketplace Listing Requirements
controls.description: Providers MUST address at least these FedRAMP rules to apply for a new FedRAMP Marketplace listing OR to request updates to an existing listing:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- Certification Data Sharing: CDS-CSO-PUB (Public Information)

controls.title: Provider Marketplace Listing Requests
controls.description: Providers MUST notify FedRAMP using the FedRAMP Marketplace Providing Listing Request Form to request a listing in the FedRAMP Marketplace.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): FedRAMP does not accept applications for a FedRAMP Marketplace Listing via email!

Related FedRAMP terms: Provider.

controls.title: Agency Use Cases
controls.description: Providers MUST demonstrate that a cloud service offering is intended for one of the following use cases:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- Direct Use: The product will be used directly by agency customers for integration into a federal information system that falls within the scope of 44 USC § 3506 and will receive an agency Authorization to Operate.
- Indirect Use: The product will be included as a third-party information resource in other cloud service offerings that are directly used by agency customers.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Cloud Service Offering, Information Resource, Provider, Third-Party Information Resource.

controls.title: Demonstrating Continuous Progress
controls.description: Providers MUST demonstrate continuous progress towards a FedRAMP Certification, documented in their Trust Center or website and updated at least quarterly; progress is measured by the provider against documented goals and milestones.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): This is an opportunity for a business to showcase its goals and progress, and should be seen as a marketing and customer experience challenge instead of a compliance challenge.

Related FedRAMP terms: Provider, Trust Center.

controls.title: Deadline for Assessment
controls.description: Providers MUST demonstrate that an assessment for a FedRAMP Certification Class B, C, or D has been scheduled within 2 years of initial listing in the Initial Implementation Phase.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Class, Provider.

controls.title: Use Instructions
controls.description: Providers MUST include instructions in the FedRAMP Certification Package that explain how to obtain and use the Secure Configuration Guide.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): These instructions may appear in a variety of ways; it is up to the provider to do so in the most appropriate and effective ways for their specific customer needs.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Package, Provider.

controls.title: Public Secure Configuration Guidance
controls.description: Providers SHOULD make the Secure Configuration Guide available publicly.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Provider.

controls.title: Recommended Secure Configuration
controls.description: Providers MUST create, maintain, and make available recommendations for securely configuring their cloud services (the Secure Configuration Guide) that includes at least the following information:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- Required: Instructions on how to securely access, configure, operate, and decommission top-level administrative accounts that control enterprise access to the entire cloud service offering.
- Required: Explanations of security-related settings that can be operated only by top-level administrative accounts and their security implications.
- Recommended: Explanations of security-related settings that can be operated only by privileged accounts and their security implications.

Related FedRAMP terms: Cloud Service Offering, Privileged Account, Provider, Top-Level Administrative Account.

Machine-readable schema: https://fedramp.gov/schemas/fedramp-certification-package-overview-schema-2026-06-24.json

controls.title: Secure Defaults
controls.description: Providers SHOULD set all settings to their recommended secure defaults for top-level administrative accounts and privileged accounts when initially provisioned.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Privileged Account, Provider, Top-Level Administrative Account.

controls.title: API Capability
controls.description: Providers SHOULD offer the capability to view and adjust security settings via an API or similar capability.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Provider.

controls.title: Comparison Capability
controls.description: Providers SHOULD offer the capability to compare all current settings for top-level administrative accounts and privileged accounts to the recommended secure defaults.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Privileged Account, Provider, Top-Level Administrative Account.

controls.title: Export Capability
controls.description: Providers SHOULD offer the capability to export all security settings in a machine-readable format.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Machine-Readable, Provider.

controls.title: Machine-Readable Guidance
controls.description: Providers SHOULD also provide the Secure Configuration Guide in a machine-readable format that can be used by customers or third-party tools to compare against current settings.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Machine-Readable, Provider.

controls.title: Versioning and Release History
controls.description: Providers SHOULD provide versioning and a release history for recommended secure default settings for top-level administrative accounts and privileged accounts as they are adjusted over time.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Privileged Account, Provider, Top-Level Administrative Account.

controls.title: Notification Requirements
controls.description: Providers MUST notify all necessary parties within 10 business days after finishing adaptive changes, also including the following information:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- Summary of any new risks identified and/or vulnerabilities resulting from the change (if applicable)

Related FedRAMP terms: Adaptive Change, All Necessary Parties, Provider, Regularly, Significant Change, Vulnerability.

controls.title: Additional Relevant Information
controls.description: Providers MAY include additional relevant information in Significant Change Notifications.
controls.guidance:
Force: MAY.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): This allows providers to convey whatever additional information they think is relevant without worrying about negative consequences from not following an exact template.

Related FedRAMP terms: Provider, Significant Change.

controls.title: Emergency Changes
controls.description: Providers MAY execute significant changes (including transformative changes) during an emergency or incident without following the Significant Change Notification rules in advance. In such emergencies, providers MUST follow all relevant procedures, notify all necessary parties, retroactively provide all Significant Change Notification materials, and complete appropriate assessment after the incident.
controls.guidance:
Force: MAY.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): Procedures for emergency changes should be documented in the FedRAMP Certification Package.

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, Certification Package, Incident, Provider, Significant Change, Transformative Change.

controls.title: Evaluate Changes
controls.description: Providers MUST evaluate all potential significant changes to determine the type of significant change and follow the appropriate Significant Change Notification rules.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- Is it a significant change? --> Continue evaluation and follow the Significant Change Notification rules.
- If it is, is it an FedRAMP Certification class change?  --> This requires a new assessment and cannot be done under the Significant Change Notification rules.
- If it is not, is it a routine recurring change? --> Follow the Routine Recurring Change rules (SCN-RTR Routine Recurring Changes).
- If it is not, is it a transformative change? --> Follow the Transformative Change rules (SCN-TRF Transformative Changes).
- If it is not, then it is an adaptive change --> Follow the Adaptive Change rules (SCN-ADP Adaptive Changes).

Related FedRAMP terms: Adaptive Change, Certification Class, Certification Class Change, Provider, Routine Recurring Change, Significant Change, Transformative Change.

Machine-readable schema: https://fedramp.gov/schemas/fedramp-significant-change-notifications-schema-2026-06-24.json

controls.title: Historical Notifications
controls.description: Providers MUST keep 12 months of historical Significant Change Notifications available with their FedRAMP Certification Data.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Data, Provider, Significant Change.

controls.title: Human and Machine-Readable Notifications
controls.description: Providers MUST make ALL Significant Change Notifications and related audit records available in human-readable and JSON formats.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Provider, Significant Change.

Machine-readable schema: https://fedramp.gov/schemas/fedramp-significant-change-notifications-schema-2026-06-24.json

controls.title: Required Information
controls.description: Providers MUST include at least the following information in Significant Change Notifications:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- Service Offering FedRAMP ID
- Assessor Name (if applicable)
- Related Vulnerability (if applicable)
- Significant Change type and explanation of categorization
- Short description of change
- Reason for change
- Summary of customer impact, including changes to services and customer configuration responsibilities
- Plan and timeline for the change, including for the verification, assessment, and/or validation of impacted Key Security Indicators or Rev5 Controls
- Copy of the business or security impact analysis
- Name and title of approver

Upstream note (verbatim): Structure of the information may vary depending on how the provider tracks this internally.

Related FedRAMP terms: Assessor, Provider, Significant Change, Validation, Verification, Vulnerability.

Machine-readable schema: https://fedramp.gov/schemas/fedramp-significant-change-notifications-schema-2026-06-24.json

controls.title: Maintain Audit Records
controls.description: Providers MUST maintain auditable records of the significant change evaluation activities required by SCN-CSO-EVA (Evaluate Changes) and make them available to FedRAMP as requested.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): These audit records must be available to FedRAMP on request; these records do not need to be included in the FedRAMP Certification Package by default and do not need to be emailed to FedRAMP continuously.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Package, Provider, Significant Change.

controls.title: Notification Mechanisms
controls.description: Providers MAY notify necessary parties in a variety of ways as long as the mechanism for notification is clearly documented in the FedRAMP Certification Package and easily accessible.
controls.guidance:
Force: MAY.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Agency, Certification Package, Provider.

controls.title: No Notification Requirements
controls.description: Providers SHOULD NOT make formal Significant Change Notifications for routine recurring changes; this type of change is exempted from notification requirements.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD NOT.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: Incident, Provider, Regularly, Routine Recurring Change, Significant Change, Vulnerability.

controls.title: Notification After Finishing
controls.description: Providers MUST notify all necessary parties within 5 business days after finishing transformative changes, including updates to all previously sent information.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, Provider, Transformative Change.

controls.title: Notification After Verification
controls.description: Providers MUST notify all necessary parties within 5 business days after completing the verification, assessment, and/or validation of transformative changes, also including the following information:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- Updates to all previously sent information
- Summary of any new risks identified and/or vulnerabilities resulting from the change (if applicable)
- Copy of the security assessment report (if applicable)

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, Provider, Transformative Change, Validation, Verification, Vulnerability.

controls.title: Notification of Final Plans
controls.description: Providers MUST notify all necessary parties of final plans for transformative changes at least 10 business days before starting transformative changes, including updates to all previously sent information.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, Provider, Transformative Change.

controls.title: Notification of Initial Plans
controls.description: Providers MUST notify all necessary parties of initial plans for transformative changes at least 30 business days before starting transformative changes, including a summary of any likely security impacts or changes in risk.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Related FedRAMP terms: All Necessary Parties, Likely, Provider, Transformative Change.

controls.title: Third-Party Review
controls.description: Providers SHOULD engage a third-party assessor to review the scope and impact of the planned change before starting transformative changes if human validation is necessary; such reviews SHOULD be limited to security decisions that require human validation.
controls.guidance:
Force: SHOULD.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): Activities that match the transformative significant change type are rare for a cloud service offering, adjusted for the size, scale, and complexity of the service. Small cloud service offerings may go years without transformative changes, while hyperscale providers may release multiple transformative changes per year.

Related FedRAMP terms: Assessor, Cloud Service Offering, Provider, Significant Change, Transformative Change, Validation.

controls.title: Update Documentation
controls.description: Providers MUST publish updated service documentation and other materials to reflect transformative changes within 30 business days after finishing transformative changes.
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Upstream note (verbatim): This requirement is focused on service documentation like user guides, information listed in the marketplace, and other such materials; it does not require updating the system security plan or FedRAMP Certification Package.

Related FedRAMP terms: Certification Package, Provider, Transformative Change.

controls.title: Rev5 Controls
controls.description: Providers MUST also include short and simple high-level summaries of at least the following for each applicable Rev5 Control:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to FedRAMP Rev 5 authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- Any organization-defined parameter values.
- Implementation status, one of Implemented, Partially Implemented, Planned, Alternative Implementation, or Not Applicable.
- The mechanisms or activities that address the control, including inheritance from another cloud service offering if applicable.
- The verification that is in place to ensure the implementation is appropriate for the control.
- The validation that is in place to ensure the implementation is working as intended.
- Independent verification.
- Independent validation.
- Any responses or clarifications to the comments in the independent verification or validation.
- Control-specific artifacts (if applicable).

Related FedRAMP terms: Artifacts, Cloud Service Offering, Provider, Validation, Verification.

controls.title: FedRAMP Rules
controls.description: Providers MUST supply a Security Decision Record, in both human-readable and JSON formats, that includes at least all of the following information for each applicable FedRAMP rule:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
- Explanation of how the rule is followed, or an explanation of the reason and resulting risk to customers for not following the rule.
- Verification that the implementation is appropriate for the rule, or that the reason for not implementing is accepted by a senior official.
- Validation that the implementation is in place and working as intended, or that the reason for not implementing is accepted by a senior official.
- Independent verification.
- Independent validation.
- Any responses or clarifications to the comments in the independent verification or validation.
- Rule-specific artifacts (if applicable).

Related FedRAMP terms: Artifacts, Provider, Security Decision Record (SDR), Validation, Verification.

Machine-readable schema: https://fedramp.gov/schemas/fedramp-security-decision-record-schema-2026-06-24.json

controls.title: Security Decision Record Metadata
controls.description: Providers MUST also include the following basic metadata in their Security Decision Record:
controls.guidance:
Force: MUST.

Applies to all FedRAMP authorizations.

Required information (upstream `following_information`, verbatim):
